title: PowerPoint for Mac: start a Copilot presentation from PowerPoint Home
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout facts, default state and documented controls are supported, and it distinguishes the Mac licensing notice from the broader Basic-tier documentation. The Intune Graph control needs only a minor clarification naming its request-body properties in the table note.

claims.quote: You can now create a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint straight from the PowerPoint Home in file menu.

claims.claim: Users can start drafting without first opening a blank or existing file.
claims.quote: helping users move from idea to first draft faster without needing to open a new file.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not resolved whether the Mac Home entry point is available to Basic users without the add-on.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Home Mac Copilot Basic licence 560536 560537 560694. Read MC1311973, Copilot overview and release notes. The notice names licensed Mac users; the overview lists Basic presentation creation; the entry-point release note specifies Web.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects Basic access without the add-on and Premium access with it, with Mac eligibility qualified in the notes.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license [...] Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is the full add-on licensed experience

claims.claim: No price specific to the Mac Home entry point is published.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Home Mac Copilot licence price meter disable; PowerPoint presentation Copilot meter credits enterprise pricing. Opened Copilot overview, release notes and Copilot pay-as-you-go meters; none names an entry-point price.

claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint presentation Copilot meter credits enterprise pricing; PowerPoint Home Mac Copilot licence price meter disable. Opened Copilot overview, release notes and Copilot pay-as-you-go meters; documented agent meters do not identify this entry point.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling content-analyzing connected experiences makes Copilot features unavailable in Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word on Mac, including this presentation-creation capability.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: [...] Excel [...] OneNote [...] Outlook [...] PowerPoint [...] Word [...] most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: The content-analysis privacy control also covers experiences such as PowerPoint Designer.
claims.quote: Connected experiences that analyze your content are experiences that use your Office content to provide you with design recommendations, editing suggestions, data insights, and similar features. For example, PowerPoint Designer or Researcher in Word.

claims.claim: The Intune preference-file route is Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > macOS > Templates > Preference file > Create > Basics > Configuration settings > Property list file.
claims.quote: Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy. [...] Platform: Select macOS [...] Templates > Preference file. [...] Select Create. [...] In Basics [...] In Configuration settings [...] Property list file

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/deviceManagement/deviceConfigurations/{deviceConfigurationId} updates the existing Intune macOSCustomAppConfiguration used for the preference.
claims.quote: Update the properties of a macOSCustomAppConfiguration object. [...] PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/deviceConfigurations/{deviceConfigurationId} [...] bundleId [...] configurationXml
claims.fix: Append to controls[2].note: 'The Graph request body sets bundleId to com.microsoft.office and configurationXml to the UTF-8 encoded preference XML containing OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference with Boolean FALSE.' These properties are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/intune-deviceconfig-macoscustomappconfiguration-update?view=graph-rest-beta and already explained in the prose.
